title: Cross-functional canary communication lifecycle sketch
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, cross-functional sketch for the communication lifecycle during canary and small-batch A/B releases. Focus: reduce noise while keeping all stakeholders informed, accelerate decision velocity, and provide a single source of truth for status and next actions.

Context / why this exists:
- We have many small LLM-driven features that need rapid iterative exposure but carry nontrivial operational risk (latency, cost spikes, behavioral regressions).
- Existing canary notes are spread across PRs, Slack threads, and on-call docs; that causes duplicated checks or missed signals.
- This doc proposes a simple cadence and templated messages for cross-team alignment (Product, SRE, Eng, Solutions, CS, Safety).

Design principles (short):
- Minimal, actionable comms: each message must include a clear ask or status (OK/Degraded/Action).
- Signal-first: telemetry + user-visible quality signal are primary; anecdotes are secondary and must be captured in a separate log.
- Owner clarity: each canary has a named steward for 72h post-exposure.
- Fast rewind: the rollback path should be one command or one config flip where possible.

Lifecycle summary (phases):
1) Preflight (T-72 to T-0)
  - Owner: feature PM + eng lead pair.
  - One-page checklist (done in PR comment and Canary ticket): capacity budget, expected token volume, fallback route, model variant mapping, monitoring dashboards, smoke test spec.
  - Slack preflight ping template to #release-orchestra (see templates).
  - Confirm canary slice(s) + sampling method (user segments, geos, percent).
2) Activation (T0 — first 6 hours)
  - Initial exposure to small cohort (0.5–2%).
  - Hourly status pings for first 6 hours with three metrics: requests/sec, p50/p95 latency delta vs baseline, quality flag (sampled eval pass rate).
  - Owner posts short digest in the canary ticket every hour.
3) Observation window (6–72 hours)
  - Cadence moves to cadence-based check-ins (6h or 12h depending on risk tier).
  - Automated anomalies should create a ticket comment and ping SRE on-call.
4) Decision & ramp (72h+)
  - If signals stable and quality within thresholds, follow ramp plan.
  - If signal breach, follow rapid mitigation (pause, reduce weight, route to fallback).

Steward responsibilities (72h after activation):
- Be reachable during working hours and check channel every 2 hours first 24h.
- Maintain the canary ticket as canonical status: initial plan, ongoing notes, final decision.
- Triage customer-facing anomalies into CS tickets and ensure follow-ups.

Signal taxonomy (quick reference):
- Health signals (SRE): 5xx rate change, pod CPU/GPU saturation, request queue length.
- Latency signals: p50/p95 absolute and delta from baseline; throttles/backpressure events.
- Cost signals: tokens/sec, token-cost-per-request spikes.
- Quality signals (Product/ML): sample-based eval pass rate, hallucination rate proxies (n-gram novelty), sentiment/regression checks.
- Human feedback: CS complaints, flagged user content.

Concrete thresholds (examples, adapt per feature):
- 5xx rate: +1% absolute or 200% relative increase -> immediate alert.
- p95 latency: +200ms absolute or 30% relative -> investigate.
- Eval pass rate drop: >5 percentage points -> pause and triage.
- Cost spike: >3x expected token cost per minute sustained for 15m -> pause.

Communication templates (copy/paste and fill):
- Preflight Slack ping (channel: #release-orchestra):
  "Preflight: [feature-name] activating canary at [T0]. Steward: @aisha. Slice: 1% global, EN-US logged-in users. TL;DR: expected 800 tpm, fallback route: model-v1. Ticket: JIRA-RLW-827. Check dashboards: link. Ask: SRE to watch infra signals for first 2h; Product to validate sample quality."

- Hourly status update (post to ticket + slack thread):
  "Hour 2 update — [feature-name] — Exposure 1% — traffic 760 req/min. Health: 5xx 0.02% (+0.01% vs baseline). Latency p95 +90ms. Eval pass: 92% (baseline 95%). Notes: one anomalous prompt flagged by CS; investigating. Next: continue sampling, raise to 2% at hour 12 if stable."

- Critical escalation ping (urgent):
  "CRITICAL: [feature-name] canary — metric [p95 latency] breached threshold at T+1:30. Immediate action: steward reducing exposure to 0.1% and swapping to fallback model-v1. On-call SRE: @ravi. Ticket: JIRA-RLW-827. Postmortem owner: eng-lead."

Fallback & rollback playbook (short):
- Preferred quick rollback order: reduce weight -> swap model variant -> disable feature flag -> revert deploy (if needed).
- Automation: a single A/B toggle in Console that sets routing to fallback variant; confirm it completes within 60s.
- Post-action telemetry check: re-evaluate 5 min after rollback to confirm baseline metrics restored.

Templates for the canary ticket body (first post):
- Title: [feature] canary — [start date/time]
- Owner: name + contact
- Steward rota: list of people and backup
- Sampling: percent, cohorts, key exclusions
- Safety nets: auto-thresholds, rollback controls, cost caps
- KPIs to watch: latency/5xx/eval pass/cost
- Links: dashboards, PR, confluence, smoke tests

Short checklist for preflight (T-72 to T-0):
- [ ] Canary ticket created and linked to PR/feature flag
- [ ] Steward assigned and backup named
- [ ] Dashboards with baseline annotated
- [ ] Smoke tests and automated checks green in testbed
- [ ] Fallback route validated in staging
- [ ] Slack preflight announcement scheduled

Operational notes & ideas to pilot (brainstorm):
- Small "signal pack" message: standard JSON payload posted to ticket every hour to make it machine-parseable.
- Canary slices that are synthetic: reserve a 0.1% synthetic cohort for deterministic evals.
- Lightweight eval harness that runs sampled responses through a small rubric (toxicity, hallucination heuristics) and uploads results to ticket.
- Weekly canary review board (15m) for ongoing features with active canaries to catch pattern failures.

Open questions / unresolved tradeoffs:
- How to balance ML-eval cadence vs. infra cadence? (ML needs more time to sample; infra wants fast signals).
- What default thresholds should be baked into console for low-friction rollouts? per-feature or global?
- How to minimize alert fatigue while still surfacing real regressions for emergent LLM failure modes?

Next steps (short):
- Pilot this lifecycle on 2 upcoming microfeatures in Feb 2025. Owners: Leah + Marco.
- Create a minimal ticket template inside Jira that populates the canary ticket body and links to dashboards. (Linked artifact: JIRA-RLW-827).
- Ship a Slack template bot that can post preflight and hourly updates when given a ticket id.

Notes to self / shorthand (informal):
- "microcommit" = 0.5–2% warm start exposure increments.
- Keep the canary ticket as canonical — do not scatter status across multiple threads.
- If in doubt: reduce exposure first, investigate second.

Appendix: quick links
- Canary dashboard example: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/xyz/feature-canary
- Canary playbook (confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RW/Canary+Playbook
- Example PR to mirror: github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/413

End.
